concept.tagline: Translating requirements into clean class hierarchies, explicit state machines, and concurrency-safe interfaces inside a service.
concept.purpose: Build a progressive mental model of Low-Level Design (LLD)—separating entities, value objects, and domain services while guarding concurrent state transitions.

spark.summary: Low-Level Design (LLD) translates high-level requirements into clean class hierarchies, explicit state machines, concurrency-safe interfaces, and extensible design patterns inside a single service or library.
spark.keyTakeaway: Great LLD isolates volatile business rules behind narrow interfaces and explicit state transitions so adding a new pricing rule, eviction policy, or booking workflow never breaks existing code.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** While High-Level Design (HLD) governs distributed services over networks, **Low-Level Design (LLD)** governs the internal architecture of a service or library: **entities** (identity + lifecycle), **value objects** (immutable.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Ticket Seat Hold Lifecycle (Replacing Boolean Flag Soup) (AVAILABLE -> HELD (TTL) -> BOOKED); Guarding Check-Then-Act in Concurrent Seat Booking (User A Thread -> Striped Seat Lock -> Seat State -> User B Thread).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Balance polymorphism against indirection, and striped locks against coarse synchronization. In production services, the LLD domain core (Entities, FSMs, Strategies) has zero framework or database imports—it depends only on narrow port interfaces (`Clock`, `SeatStore`.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Practice full end-to-end LLD implementations across caching, scheduling, and concurrency.

learningJourney.title: What is Low-Level System Design (LLD)
learningJourney.explanation:
While High-Level Design (HLD) governs distributed services over networks, **Low-Level Design (LLD)** governs the internal architecture of a service or library: **entities** (identity + lifecycle), **value objects** (immutable, equality by value), and **stateless domain services**.

Clean LLD models lifecycles as **explicit Finite State Machines (FSMs)** and isolates volatile rules behind **Strategy, State, Observer, and Command** interfaces.

learningJourney.title: Why boolean flags and check-then-act races break services
learningJourney.explanation:
Poor LLD produces god classes, brittle `if-else` trees, and concurrency bugs at 100k+ lines of code.

Two failure modes recur constantly: **boolean flag explosion** (`isActive`, `isPaused`, `isDeleted` allowing illegal states) and **check-then-act race conditions** where two threads both see `spot.isFree() == true` and issue duplicate tickets.

sectionDiagram.summary: Making check-and-reserve atomic under a per-entity lock or optimistic CAS prevents double-booking.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why should an LLD Seat or Order entity replace independent booleans (isHeld, isBooked, isCancelled) with a single enum-backed State Machine?

options.text: Enums take less RAM than booleans in Java
options.feedback: The motivation is state integrity, not a few bytes of memory.

options.text: A single enum state with explicit transitions makes impossible combinations (e.g., isHeld=true and isBooked=true) unrepresentable
options.feedback: Correct: an explicit FSM guarantees every entity is in exactly one valid state at any moment.

options.text: Enums automatically make the class thread-safe without locks
options.feedback: State transitions still require atomic locking or CAS under concurrency.

beginner.byteSummary:
**The Core Idea (Beginner):** While High-Level Design (HLD) governs distributed services over networks, **Low-Level Design (LLD)** governs the internal architecture of a service or library: **entities** (identity + lifecycle), **value objects**.

**How It Flows:** Think of Low-Level System Design: LRU Cache, Elevator & Ticket Booking as a clear step-by-step chain: AVAILABLE -> HELD (TTL) -> BOOKED -> User A Thread -> Striped Seat Lock.

**Why Beginners Should Care:** Great LLD isolates volatile business rules behind narrow interfaces and explicit state transitions so adding a new pricing rule, eviction policy, or booking workflow never breaks existing code.

_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
